A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Singular Value Calibration (SVC) work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching the relocated appendix results.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision and language merging experiments, ablations, targeted calibration results, and computational measurements. Section 5.1 explicitly attributes the reported results to the authors' own runs.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a 20-task merging comparison and further computational measurements in Table 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The SVD, task-response projections, clipped coefficient aggregation, singular-value rescaling, and reconstruction remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1. The IA3 vector extension already appears in v1's appendix. Renaming column/row space as output/input space does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C/Table 5 adds a joint 20-task CV merging scenario beyond the reported 8-task and 14-task settings, testing preservation of more tasks within one merged model. Its dataset membership is unspecified, so particular newly covered datasets or domains cannot be identified. Existing NLP coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The new 20-task comparison evaluates Subspace-Boosted and TALL Mask with and without SVC; both were cited but not evaluated in v1. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, including the existing CAT and STAR comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds end-to-end timing of base mergers with and without SVC across ViT-B/32, LLaMA2-7B, and BERT, and extends resource measurements to Qwen2.5-7B. Existing accuracy metrics and stated settings remain unchanged. The main-text statement fixing lambda to 1 repeats information already present in v1's appendix.

E4.justification: Appendix C/Table 6 adds an analysis of SVC's computational overhead relative to each base merger, extending v1's standalone SVC cost analysis. The alpha sensitivity study, targeted-task calibration heatmap, and left-versus-right singular-vector ablation remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for its empirical comparisons. The new results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All matched pre-existing accuracy results are unchanged, including v1 Tables 5–13 retained as v2 Tables 7–15. New Table 5 reports, for example, Subspace-Boosted at 68.89% without SVC versus 71.47% with SVC, and TALL Mask at 37.94% versus 54.41%. Table 6 adds end-to-end runtimes, while Table 4 adds Qwen2.5-7B measurements of 249.3 seconds and 2,513.1 MiB.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds an explicit multi-task output-space matching objective in Eq. (24) and contrasts it with projection matching. Lemma 3.2, Theorem 3.3, and the operative calibration equations remain unchanged. The rewritten response equations in Section 3.2 are equivalent explanations of the existing projections.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims: spectral over-counting causes imbalance, SVC provides training-free and data-free singular-value calibration, and it improves vision and language merging. The headline 13.0% Task Arithmetic improvement is unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds the explanation that merged input directions can mix patterns from several tasks and be less representative of individual experts. Appendix C interprets the 20-task results as supporting larger-scale applicability. v2 also removes v1's explicit limitation concerning untested video-understanding, federated-aggregation, and continual-learning applications.

D1.justification: Figures 2 and 4 newly identify their diagnostic setting as 8-task CV classification, and the additional cost measurements expand resource information. Existing hardware, alpha defaults, lambda setting, layer-specific BERT treatment, IA3 details, and code-access information are retained. The new 20-task comparison does not specify its precise dataset composition or backbone.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a dedicated spectral-space discussion, and Appendix B substantially expands positioning against Iso-style methods and Subspace-Boosting. It also introduces connections to SVCCA/CKA, redundancy reduction, lottery-ticket research, compression, retrieval, and cross-subject alignment, with corresponding new citations. This substantially broadens the research context beyond v1's existing TSV/Iso discussion.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 is rewritten around output responses, column/row terminology becomes output/input terminology, and the original single appendix is reorganized into implementation, analysis, and experiments sections. Related-work explanations, acknowledgements, an impact statement, and affiliation/publication text are added or revised. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5 and 6, extends Table 4 with a Qwen row, and clarifies several figure captions. Existing appendix tables are relocated and renumbered, with changed page packing. All six figures retain their plotted or illustrated content, and existing result-table structures are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The 20-task comparison and end-to-end timing table provide useful additional evidence about larger merges and practical cost, while the expanded spectral-method discussion clarifies positioning. These are incremental gains over v1's already substantial empirical evidence. Their value is limited by missing details for the 20-task setup and unchanged absence of uncertainty reporting; removing the explicit untested-applications limitation also weakens qualification of scope.
